description: Accidental data loss response: a developer accidentally dropped a production PostgreSQL table containing 10M rows of customer data. Must: immediately stop all writes to the database to prevent overwriting WAL, identify the exact deletion timestamp from logs, restore the database to a point-in-time (PITR) just before deletion, reconcile any data created after the restore point (re-apply from application logs), verify data integrity, and implement preventive controls (table-level drop protection, stricter RBAC). Risk factors: WAL retention window expiring before restore, data created after deletion point being lost, PITR restore overwriting other concurrent changes. Tools available: pg_basebackup, wal-g, aws RDS, psql, ansible.
